//: Mutation matrix for probe_crossfade (issue #141). Every mutant breaks ONE of the rules Crossfade.h owns and must turn the probe red; a SURVIVOR means the assertion guarding that rule is inert and the rule is unprotected. The suppressions are the ones that matter — #141 says a crossfade in the wrong place is vandalism, so 'when NOT to' is what these break. Driven by native/tools/mutate.py (never a hand-rolled loop; see CONTRIBUTING).

mutants.name: drop-the-same-album-suppression
mutants.//: THE headline rule. Without it two tracks of one live record are crossfaded, which is the exact thing #141 calls vandalism.

mutants.name: same-album-compares-case-sensitively
mutants.//: Two rips of one disc by different taggers spell the album differently in case/padding. A case-sensitive compare silently un-suppresses exactly those.

mutants.name: one-side-tagged-falls-through-to-the-folder
mutants.//: Dropping the 'either side tagged' gate lets an untagged stray in an album folder suppress a boundary whose tags disagree — the folder overriding a tag, which the fallback must never do.

mutants.name: drop-the-untagged-folder-fallback
mutants.//: The one rule #141 does not spell out, kept separable on purpose. Without it a folder of untagged rips of one album is crossfaded.

mutants.name: empty-folders-count-as-the-same-record
mutants.//: Two entries with no folder (streams, unresolvable paths) are not evidence of one record; matching them would suppress every boundary between two of them.

mutants.name: drop-the-audiobook-carve-out
mutants.//: The carve-out shared with ReplayGain. Without it a chapter's last sentence dissolves into the next chapter's first, and video would fade too (isMusic is false for video through the same host expression).

mutants.name: clamp-off-becomes-one-second
mutants.//: Where the off state ACTUALLY lives. secondsFor's `want <= 0` early exit is redundant by construction (clampSeconds has already produced 0, and 0 is below the minimum anyway), so breaking THAT line is an equivalent mutant and says nothing; breaking clampSeconds' off case is the real thing — an install that never asked for crossfade would start getting a one-second one.

mutants.name: no-cap-on-the-outgoing-track
mutants.//: A 12 s window over a 9 s skit is two tracks played at once, not a transition.

mutants.name: no-cap-on-the-incoming-track
mutants.//: The mirror. The shorter of the two sides has to win, not just the outgoing one.

mutants.name: unknown-length-caps-to-zero
mutants.//: durationSec 0 means 'the container would not tell us cheaply'. Treating it as a real length turns that into 'never fade' — the guard is the > 0.0, and this proves it is load-bearing.

mutants.name: ship-a-sub-second-blip
mutants.//: A window the cap has shrunk under a second is a blip, not a transition, and is dropped.

mutants.name: linear-ramp-instead-of-equal-power
mutants.//: The obvious wrong curve. out + in == 1 looks right on paper and dips to 0.707 of full power at the midpoint; the probe's out^2 + in^2 == 1 assertion is the only thing that tells the two apart.

mutants.name: unclamped-curve-runs-past-the-window
mutants.//: A tick that overshoots must land on the end of the fade, not back up the other side of the quarter-cycle.
mutants.replace:
const double x = t;
        return std::sin(x * 3.14159265358979323846 / 2.0);

mutants.name: clamp-rounds-a-stray-value-down-to-off
mutants.//: clampSeconds must round UP to the minimum, never down to off: a settings surface showing the feature as on must not be lying about it.

mutants.name: settings-default-is-not-off
mutants.//: #141 makes crossfade opt-in (unlike ReplayGain). An absent key must read 0, or every existing install starts crossfading after an update.

mutants.name: settings-does-not-clamp-on-write
mutants.//: An out-of-band value written into the user's ini is one a getter's clamp would hide rather than fix.

mutants.name: channel-pick-beats-the-queue-successor
mutants.//: Channel mode (#141). The precedence is the rule: consulting the channel's next pick while the queue still has entries left would overlap the record now playing with the channel's next item several tracks early - the wrong file, at the wrong time, over music with four minutes left to run. It also un-suppresses the same-album boundary the queue successor would have been refused for.

mutants.name: the-last-entry-is-not-a-channel-boundary
mutants.//: An off-by-one the other way: with <=, the LAST entry still reads as having a successor, the channel's pick is never consulted, and channel mode silently keeps the behaviour #141 asked to change (no fade, ever) while looking wired up.

mutants.name: drop-the-channel-pick
mutants.//: The whole of what channel mode adds. Without it the end of a queue is always the end of the music and no channel boundary can ever open a window.
mutants.find: return channelNext;                                       // the last entry: the channel's, or nothing
mutants.replace: return QString();                                         // the last entry: the channel's, or nothing

mutants.name: name-a-boundary-with-nothing-playing
mutants.//: A stray call during a teardown - no current track, or an empty queue - must not name a file. Without the guard, curIndex -1 reads as 'has a successor' and hands back an entry from a queue that is not playing.
mutants.find: if (curIndex < 0 || queueCount <= 0) return QString();   // nothing is playing: no boundary to have
mutants.replace: if (false)                           return QString();   // nothing is playing: no boundary to have
